transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-10-01 15:00 PDT · 48 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Jared Cole (Orion CTO), Maya Lim (Orion Security Lead), Omar Farouk (Orion DevOps), Lena Park (PM)

Summary: Quick intros, then deep dive on security posture for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Lots of Qs about SOC2/ISO artifacts, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS.

00:00 Jared Cole: hey thanks everyone for jumping on, uh we wanted to run through Redwood's security posture before we show to our procurement team
00:12 Aisha Patel: yeah thanks Jared, appreciate it. we'll do a quick intro, then Carlos will walk through the security controls and options — hosted, dedicated, private — and then we'll capture any gaps.
00:25 Carlos Nguyen: hey all, Carlos here, redwood systems engineer. quick note: i'll call out some of the specifics like SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001, SAML, SCIM, RBAC, audit logging, and KMS integration. feel free to stop me.
00:40 Maya Lim: great, our goals: we handle regulated customer data, need to know if we can use hosted or if we need dedicated/private due to data residency and encryption at rest keys. also SSO and auditability are must-haves.
00:55 Aisha Patel: got it. high level — redwood's hosted tier is our fastest onramp, we do SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001, and we can provide certs. dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and stronger isolation. private is VPC/on-prem where you control the network and keys.
01:18 Jared Cole: can you confirm where logs live for hosted? like full request/response logs — retention, access controls?
01:28 Carlos Nguyen: yeah so for hosted by default we retain structured audit logs in our control plane for 90 days, access is RBAC-controlled and available via console and API. for customers that need longer retention we have add-on retention packages or you can stream logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 export.
01:45 Maya Lim: is the request/response payload included or redacted? we have PHI in some payloads so that matters.
01:53 Carlos Nguyen: good question. by default we redact sensitive fields on ingestion if you use our standard SDKs and masking rules, but you can also opt-out if you run dedicated/private and manage retention yourself. for hosted we recommend tokenization and redaction; we can also enable field-level redaction as a configuration.
02:12 Omar Farouk: about encryption — we need to bring our own key, KMS/HSM, for at-rest encryption in private deployments. what's supported?
02:21 Carlos Nguyen: private supports customer-managed keys via KMS and bring-your-own-HSM integrations; we support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and Vault HSM in private or dedicated with extra ops config. hosted supports our managed KMS but we also offer a BYOK option for enterprise contracts.
02:37 Lena Park: timeline question — if we choose dedicated, how long to provision and are there audit controls for tenant isolation?
02:45 Aisha Patel: dedicated provisioning is typically a few weeks depending on capacity and region. you get dedicated GPU nodes and network isolation; we also provide additional logging, per-tenant RBAC, and support for private subnets.
03:02 Jared Cole: on SSO — we use SAML with SSO and SCIM for provisioning. how mature is your SAML implementation? can we map groups to roles?
03:12 Carlos Nguyen: yes, SAML SSO is supported across all tiers. SCIM provisioning to sync users and groups automates deprovisioning. you can map SAML attributes or SCIM groups to Redwood roles (admin, developer, auditor) — that's how RBAC is enforced.
03:28 Maya Lim: do you support session length controls, forced MFA, and audit of SSO events?
03:33 Carlos Nguyen: session and token TTLs are configurable in enterprise plans; we enforce MFA on certain roles and surface SSO event logs in the audit stream.
03:45 Jared Cole: audit logs — what fields are recorded? do they include token-level costs and model route used?
03:53 Carlos Nguyen: audit logs capture user, action, timestamp, resource, request metadata (route, model), and we can include token-level billing metadata in a separate usage stream. full request/response payloads are optional and handled per retention policy.
04:10 Maya Lim: ISO27001 — do you have a statement of applicability or scope doc?
04:15 Aisha Patel: yes, we'll share our ISO27001 scope and SOC 2 Type II report in the follow-up. those are standard artifacts we provide under NDA.
04:25 Omar Farouk: network architecture for private — do you support VPC peering or is it an appliance? also curious about egress rules and dedicated private endpoints.
04:35 Carlos Nguyen: private supports VPC peering and private endpoints; we also provide an on-prem package as an air-gapped option. egress is configurable, and we can set up strict security groups, NAT gateways or restrict egress entirely and use S3 endpoints for log export.
04:52 Jared Cole: is there an option to keep all data in our region for compliance?
04:58 Carlos Nguyen: yes, for private deployments you run in your VPC/region. dedicated can be pinned to a region. hosted can be regionalized — we have regional hosted endpoints and data residency controls for enterprise customers.
05:14 Maya Lim: about the runtime: do you ever cache KV or prefix tokens that could be accessible across customers? that's a big concern for us.
05:25 Carlos Nguyen: no cross-tenant KV cache sharing. we do caching and prefix caching per-tenant to improve performance, but isolation is enforced at runtime. in dedicated/private you can also disable caching if you want.
05:40 Jared Cole: there was a question from procurement about indemnity and logs for audits — can you provide chain-of-custody for model outputs?
05:51 Aisha Patel: we provide tamper-evident audit logs with timestamps and signatures for enterprise agreements. we can also offer exportable immutable archives for audits.
06:07 Lena Park: what's the rollback strategy for model rollouts? we want reproducibility for a model version used in production in case of incidents.
06:16 Carlos Nguyen: rollouts are versioned; we keep model versioning metadata and can pin routing policies. you can reproduce inference by pinning a model snapshot and seed; we also store per-request model_id in the audit logs for tracing.
06:32 Maya Lim: do you have penetration test reports or third-party attestation?
06:36 Aisha Patel: yes, we do annual pentests and we share summary reports under NDA. we also have vulnerability management and CVE tracking.
06:46 Omar Farouk: for dedicated, if we want BYOK, how do we manage key rotation without downtime?
06:53 Carlos Nguyen: we support key rotation workflows that use envelope encryption; rotations can be staged so there's no downtime. for HSMs we follow NIST best practices and provide rotation automation.
07:07 Jared Cole: any known limitations for on-prem in terms of model sizes or quantization?
07:13 Carlos Nguyen: on-prem package supports our runtime but you need sufficient GPU capacity for large models; some quantization paths may require specific kernels — we'll validate in the pilot.
07:26 Maya Lim: incident response — what's your SLA for breach notification and support tiers?
07:31 Aisha Patel: we have tiered incident response SLAs in our enterprise contracts; standard is 72 hours notification for incidents, but enterprise contracts have faster timelines and dedicated escalation. we'll share the policy.
07:47 Jared Cole: how do we validate that deletions are enforced? e.g., data retention requests, right to be forgotten?
07:54 Carlos Nguyen: we support programmatic data deletion and can provide deletion proof. for hosted we have retention TTLs; for private you control retention and deletion.
08:05 Maya Lim: curious about pys? typo? (laughs) i mean PKI for cert rotation on endpoints — what's your approach?
08:12 Carlos Nguyen: we use automated cert rotation for service endpoints and can integrate with your PKI for mTLS if needed.
08:22 Lena Park: any blockers we should flag for procurement or legal?
08:26 Aisha Patel: pc: procurement typically asks for SOC2, ISO, indemnity language, and data processing addendum. legal often wants KMS terms and a clear data residency clause.
08:40 Jared Cole: okay, can you put together a one-pager that maps our requirements to your controls?
08:45 Aisha Patel: yes, we can do a security mapping doc and send SOC2/ISO certs.
08:50 Maya Lim: for SSO mapping to RBAC — can we have custom roles beyond admin/dev/auditor? we need least privilege for operators.
08:58 Carlos Nguyen: yes, roles are customizable; we support fine-grained policies and resource scoping.
09:07 Omar Farouk: benchmark question — if we run a workload with our ACU, can you instrument latencies per token and GPU utilization?
09:15 Carlos Nguyen: yes, our telemetry includes per-request latency, token counts, GPU utilization and cost breakdown per model route. we'll instrument during the pilot and share dashboards.
09:29 Jared Cole: any final items we should know?
09:32 Aisha Patel: we'll follow up with artifacts and schedule a private deep-dive.
09:35 Lena Park: thanks, that covers it.

Recap/Next Steps (end of call):
- Aisha: send SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 certs and security mapping (by 2026-10-05)
- Carlos: share SAML/SCIM docs, sample metadata, and pilot instrumentation plan (by 2026-10-04)
- Omar/Maya: provide network diagram, compliance checklist and constraints (by 2026-10-06)
- Schedule Private deep-dive and Dedicated pilot planning session (propose times by 2026-10-03)

Notes: Transcription may have small errors in proper nouns or acronyms; audio had mild overlap at times.
